players.product: MRSI high-precision die bonders for packaging optical components into transceivers (Global Technologies division)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results (CEO Anders Lindqvist / CFO Pierre Brorsson): order intake up 10% to almost SEK 2.7 billion against a very strong Q3 2025, with the greatest contribution from High Volume and Global Technologies; net sales up 38% to almost SEK 2.4 billion, with double-digit growth in all divisions, primarily driven by Global Technologies; gross margin 52%; EBIT SEK 610 million (26% margin); record order backlog of a little more than SEK 5.5 billion. CFO: record aftermarket revenue of SEK 606 million in the quarter; rolling 12-month sales SEK 9.3 billion with a 28% EBIT margin, with aftermarket above SEK 2 billion, 24% of net sales. Cash position SEK 2.9 billion (cash at the end of the period above SEK 3 billion); investments mainly in facilities being built in Taiwan and China.
quarterly_data.figure: orders almost SEK 2.7 billion (+10%); net sales almost SEK 2.4 billion (+38%); gross margin 52%; EBIT SEK 610 million (26%); backlog a little more than SEK 5.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: New full-year 2026 outlook from the Board of Directors: net sales of SEK 9.75 billion. CFO: the raise is broad based - apart from Pattern Generators, where the company has a longer view of quarterly sales, it sees a little better sales in all other divisions than earlier in the year. New financial targets were launched at the Capital Markets Day on August 31. CFO on R&D: 'The growth rate is likely to decline, but the level is not going to decline.'
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales outlook SEK 9.75 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Global Technologies (die bonding, PCB test): orders up 33% to a bit more than SEK 1 billion; sales more than doubled, up 105% to SEK 852 million; gross margin 60% on volume and a very favorable product mix (high aftermarket and software share); EBIT SEK 359 million, 42% margin, including a SEK 15 million revaluation of a consideration in Surfx; backlog SEK 2.3 billion, more than doubled. CEO: market conditions remain very strong, driven by investments in AI infrastructure, in developing advanced packaging and in defense. CEO: the exceptional part is the record gross margin, and Q4 will already show somewhat different numbers. CEO: good momentum in both PCB test and die bonding; quarter-on-quarter the strongest order intake was on the die-bonding side, whereas PCB test had been the strongest driver earlier in the year. CFO, asked whether Global Technologies' visibility to the beginning of 2028 had changed: 'Not materially changed. We do not really take orders so much beyond that in Global Technologies.' CFO: Plasma Solutions looks very promising and interest in 3D nanoprinting is growing, still to materialize.
quarterly_data.figure: orders a bit more than SEK 1 billion (+33%); sales SEK 852 million (+105%); gross margin 60%; EBIT SEK 359 million (42%); backlog SEK 2.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (CEO / CFO): PCB test lead times are a bit longer than the company would wish; the capacity extension keeps its time plan - CFO: 'We will be ready beginning of the year, and I think with some trimming towards the end of the first quarter, we will have about a 25% capacity increase.' CEO: the company is already producing more through supply-chain and factory productivity work, and 'we haven't made any substantial losses based on lead times.' Sourcing (CEO): no sourcing or availability effect so far despite price increases around the industry; freight and other cost increases are likely and the intention is to pass them on to customers. CEO: non-reversible down payments are required at order, there have been no cancellations or delivery-date changes, and 'Everyone wants it earlier.'
quarterly_data.figure: about a 25% PCB-test capacity increase (ready at the beginning of the year, trimmed toward the end of the first quarter)

quarterly_data.signal: Pattern Generators: two new products launched at the Capital Markets Day that the CEO says expand the available market - SLX Kite, a next-generation semiconductor mask writer, and IQX, a photomask inspection machine for the semiconductor segment. CEO on IQX: customer interest is really high, the product is developed with some key customers, and the first tools ship to customers around this time ('if not yet already happened'); it targets the mature-node segment, which the CEO says competitors focused on small nodes have left as a gap, with better cost of ownership and productivity (company view). CFO on SLX Kite: great interest in a market with basically two large players; 'Positive reception, but jury is still out there.'
quarterly_data.figure: first IQX tools shipping to customers around the time of the call

quarterly_data.signal: Pattern Generators Q3 2026: order intake down to SEK 616 million with three tools ordered - one Prexision 80 Evo display mask writer and two SLX semiconductor mask writers; sales up 20% to SEK 580 million, including SEK 23 million from the recently acquired Cowin; gross margin 59%; EBIT SEK 188 million (32% margin), including a negative SEK 13 million effect from the Cowin acquisition; backlog of 11 systems worth SEK 1.741 billion. CEO on display: no macro factor behind the quieter display orders, rather timing and normalization; foldable phones and advanced displays with automatic privacy filters drive the need for advanced masks; display mask-writer replacement need is typically two, three machines per year. CEO: semiconductor mask-writer demand is quite stable and should continue, or maybe even increase, into next year.
quarterly_data.figure: orders SEK 616 million; sales SEK 580 million (+20%); EBIT SEK 188 million (32%); backlog 11 systems, SEK 1.741 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 12-inch photomasks (CEO): the normal semiconductor photomask is 6 in; TSMC and ASML, with some other players in the industry, are now coming together to set a 12-in photomask format intended for the smallest nodes (the CEO confirmed this reaches down to 2 nm). On small nodes about 75% of photomasks can be laser-written and only 25% need electron-beam writing. The SLX was developed to handle 12-in photomasks from the beginning, so the adaptation is small, and the company believes it is very well positioned to capture at least the laser-written 12-in masks. The timing of orders is hard to say ('Everything has to go in sync'); the ASP 'should be higher'; the whole installed base is 6-in.
quarterly_data.figure: 75% of small-node photomasks laser-writable; 25% need electron beam

quarterly_data.signal: PCB Assembly Solutions: demand in the high-mix, low-volume segment remains soft, with price pressure especially from Japanese competitors; order intake SEK 367 million (-9%); sales up 14% to SEK 358 million; gross margin 41%, helped by stronger U.S. sales; EBIT SEK 42 million (12% margin); backlog SEK 266 million. CFO on the restructuring program: around SEK 100 million of cost taken out at the end, a long-term project; more than half of the charges have been taken and the vast majority of the rest is likely to be taken in Q4. High Volume (dispensing): very good demand outside China while China's domestic market weakened a little (a typical seasonal pattern, with most orders in the first half); order intake up 42% to a little above SEK 600 million; sales SEK 569 million; gross margin 41%; EBIT SEK 74 million (13% margin) after SEK 25 million of ESOP costs; backlog SEK 1.2 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: PCB Assembly Solutions orders SEK 367 million (-9%), EBIT SEK 42 million; High Volume orders a little above SEK 600 million (+42%), EBIT SEK 74 million, backlog SEK 1.2 billion
